reason: Plural of 'root thorn' (R2996), which is accepted with 'root spine' (R2997). Ringed, hardened, pointed roots on palm trunks and bamboo culm nodes are roots that grow from the shoot and turned into spines, which is PO's definition. There is no further problem beyond what the accepted singular already covers.

The persistent protonemal flaps or appendages of mosses such as Tetraphis are leaf-like plates of protonema tissue, not separate organs. PO_0030003 lists 'portion of protonema tissue' as a synonym, so a flap is a portion of protonema. PO has no finer protonema part apart from cell types. Persistence and shape are qualities of it.
Spelling variant of R3001 ('protonemal' for 'protonematal'); same reasoning.

In floras, 'basal sinus' nearly always means the notch at the base of a cordate, sagittate or peltate blade (Araceae, Nymphaea, Piper), which is leaf sinus PO_0025384. On a calyx, corolla or other phyllome, the sinus should go to phyllome sinus (PO_0025383), not leaf sinus. So the rule should apply only to leaf parts.

PO has no 'secretory cavity' class. Resin canal (PO_0005665) is an elongate duct and oil gland/oil cavity (PO_0005669) is for oil. The accepted rules already map resin gland (R2721) and resin dots (R3267) to PO_0005656, and a resin pocket is the same thing seen as a lined cavity. This is the closest existing class and matches the precedent.
Same as R3010. A non-elongate resin cavity has no closer PO class. Resin canal is a duct and oil cavity is for oil.
Plural of R3010, same reasoning.

In floras, a sporangiaster is a sterile, modified sporangium with a glandular head, found among the sporangia of some Polypodiaceae such as Pleopeltis and Polypodium. It is a kind of sporangium, with sterility as a quality. The fungal sense does not occur in plant floras.
Plural of R3013, same reasoning.

A modified sporangium is still a sporangium. 'Modified' only says it is unusual (sterile, glandular), and in these floras it is the same structure as the sporangiaster. Sporangiophores are covered by their own rule (R3272, sporophyll), so this rule does not take them.

Inflorescence bract is wrong. In Asteraceae (Ambrosia, Iva, Parthenium), 'pistillate paleae' are receptacle chaff, which is flower bract PO_0009034 (synonym chaff, as in R0121). In grasses, a palea of a pistillate floret is palea PO_0009038. The word alone does not tell which, so no single target is safe.
Singular of R3016, same ambiguity between Asteraceae chaff (PO_0009034) and the grass palea (PO_0009038). Inflorescence bract is wrong for both.
Same as R3016. Paleae of florets are either receptacle chaff (flower bract) or grass paleae (PO_0009038), never inflorescence bracts. The phrase does not show which family is meant.

'Pseudumbel leaves' is a Euphorbia term for the whorl of leaf-like bracts at the base of the terminal pseudumbel. These are inflorescence bracts, and the word itself already names the inflorescence, so a constraint adds nothing. 'Leave' is a word-ending error for 'leaf'.
Same as R3019. The term already names the pseudumbel, so it cannot be misapplied.
Plural of R3020, same reasoning.

'Ray leaves' is the standard Euphorbia term (Flora Zambesiaca, Flora of Tropical East Africa) for the bracts below the rays of the pseudumbel, which are inflorescence bracts. 'Ray' (R2801) already handles umbel rays as axes. No other common flora sense of 'ray leaf' was found, so a constraint is not needed.

In moss floras (Pottiaceae: Barbula, Tortula, Didymodon), 'peristome filaments' are the 32 filiform, often twisted peristome teeth. The accepted 'filiform peristome teeth' (R3026) shows the same treatment. Endostome segments and cilia are called 'segments' or 'cilia', not filaments, and the endostome has its own class (FLOPO_0986064).
Plural of R3024, same reasoning.

Ambiguous: it can mean a seedling's first leaf or the lowest leaf of a shoot or culm. The seedling sense is already covered by 'seedling leaf' (R3716), which maps to 'vascular leaf part of seedling' and notes that juvenile vascular leaf PO_0006339 is a stage class, not the seedling's leaf. Without that context, this rule would mislabel lowest leaves.
Same ambiguity as R3027 (seedling leaf versus lowest leaf). The juvenile-stage class is not the right target for the seedling sense either.
Plural of R3028, same reasoning.

This follows the accepted precedents 'glandular dot(s)' (R2739/R2740) and 'taches glanduleuses' / 'macules glanduleuses' (R3241/R3242), all mapped to PO_0005656. A glandular spot is a flat gland seen as a spot. Its density and colour belong to the gland, and the surface value 'gland-dotted' stays separate.
French singular of the accepted 'taches glanduleuses' (R3241), mapped to the same class.
Spelling variant of 'tache glanduleuse'. Same precedent (R3241).
Plural of R3030. Same precedent as 'glandular dots' (R2740).

The accepted corona filament rules (R2642-R2644) say explicitly that 'outer/inner series can be left to context'. Inner tepals going to tepal is the same kind of decision. 'Inner' is a position, not a separate kind of part, and there is no inner corona lobe class.
Same as R3034. This follows the corona filament and inner tepal precedents.
Same as R3034.

'Coccu' is the lemmatizer's truncation of 'coccus'. 'Coccus' and 'cocci' (R2246/R2247) are already accepted as mericarp, because a coccus is the one-seeded mericarp of a schizocarp. The match key is a whole word, so it will not catch other words, and a constraint would add nothing.
